policyDetail.purpose: This policy establishes the group-wide requirements and minimum standards for {category} across all APAC entities. It defines roles, mandatory controls, and the exception process, and applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties acting on behalf of the group.
policyDetail.standardNote: Policy documents are not held in a single house format, so the platform standardises only the record fields. The authoritative content is the attached document — read it in the viewer below or download the original file.
policyDetail.doc.cover.appliesToValue: All APAC operating companies, employees, contractors and external parties
policyDetail.doc.p2.title: 1. Purpose and scope
policyDetail.doc.p2.para1: This policy establishes the group-wide requirements and minimum standards for {category} matters across all Ricoh Asia Pacific operating companies. It defines the mandatory requirements, the roles accountable for them, and the process for requesting an exception.
policyDetail.doc.p2.para2: It applies to all information assets within the scope of the information security management system, whether owned by Ricoh or entrusted to Ricoh by a customer or business partner, and to all employees, contractors and external parties acting on behalf of the company.
policyDetail.doc.p2.para3: Where local law or a regulator imposes a stricter requirement, the stricter requirement prevails and the difference is recorded in the operating company ISMS profile.
policyDetail.doc.p2.head: 2. Roles and responsibilities
policyDetail.doc.p2.b1: The Information Security Committee approves this policy and reviews it at least annually.
policyDetail.doc.p2.b2: The Regional Information Security Officer maintains the policy and monitors compliance across the region.
policyDetail.doc.p2.b3: Operating company Information Security Officers implement the policy locally and report exceptions.
policyDetail.doc.p2.b4: Asset owners apply the controls relevant to the assets they own.
policyDetail.doc.p3.title: 3. Policy statements
policyDetail.doc.p3.para1: The requirements below are mandatory. Each statement is mapped to one or more Annex A controls of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and is tested as part of the regional control testing programme.
policyDetail.doc.p3.n1: Information is classified and handled according to the group classification scheme.
policyDetail.doc.p3.n2: Access to information and information processing facilities is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed at least twice a year.
policyDetail.doc.p3.n3: Multi-factor authentication is required for all remote and privileged access.
policyDetail.doc.p3.n4: Security events are reported through the incident process without delay and are classified S1 to S3 on submission.
policyDetail.doc.p3.n5: External parties are risk-assessed before access is granted and re-assessed at the agreed interval.
policyDetail.doc.p3.n6: Changes to production systems follow the documented change process with segregation of duties.
policyDetail.doc.p4.title: 4. Compliance and exceptions
policyDetail.doc.p4.para1: Compliance is measured through control testing, internal audit, and the annual attestation cycle. Results are reported to the Information Security Committee as part of the Security Metric Program.
policyDetail.doc.p4.para2: An exception must be requested in writing, carry a business justification, a compensating control and an expiry date, and be approved by the Regional Information Security Officer. Exceptions are recorded in the register and reviewed at expiry.
policyDetail.doc.p4.head: 5. Review and maintenance
policyDetail.doc.p4.b1: Reviewed at least once a year, or after a significant security incident or organisational change.
policyDetail.doc.p4.b2: Superseded versions are retained for three years in the controlled document store.
policyDetail.doc.p4.b3: The master copy is held on the regional intranet; printed copies are uncontrolled.
